exercise.name: Seated Barbell Calf Raise
library_steps: Sit on a bench and set the front of both feet on a block.
Rest a padded barbell across your lower thighs and hold it steady.
Raise your heels as high as you can, then lower slowly for a stretch.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated on a bench, the balls of both feet on a block, a bar across the lower thighs; the heels drop, then rise as high as they go. Soleus (calves) does the work.

setup.target: Seated, knees bent ~90 deg, forefoot on a ~8 cm block.
setup.why: Library step 1; KINO seated condition at knee 90 deg.

setup.target: Across both lower thighs near the knees, held by both hands.

muscles.emg: Seated calf raises grew the soleus (+2.9 %) but hardly the gastrocnemius (KINO).

sources.citation: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, et al. 2023. Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training. Front Physiol 14:1272106.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated (knee 90 deg) vs standing calf raises, 12 weeks: in the seated leg the soleus grew (+2.9 %) but the gastrocnemius barely did (+0.6-1.7 %): seated calf raises work the soleus.

sources.citation: Binstead JT, Varacallo MA. 2026. Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb: Calf. StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf).
sources.what_it_gave: The calf (posterior lower leg) holds the muscles that plantarflex the ankle (raise the heel).

clip_check.check: Forefoot on the block, heels down then up
Bar on the thighs, both hands on it
